subject: Commitment staging & burst quota — sizing details request
messages:
From: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@mlmarket.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@mlmarket.io
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated commit staging & burst profile — initial details

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We want to firm up the dedicated commitment shape and how burst credits are applied across stages (pilot -> ramp -> steady). Before legal completes SOW language, procurement asked for a short technical appendix that lists the traffic assumptions you used to size the reserved GPU footprint. Can you send a short questionnaire or template to capture: average requests/s (p95), expected sustained QPS during business hours, peak burst QPS and burst duration, typical prompt / response token lengths, session/ KV-cache expectations, and whether longer context windows (8k/32k) will be used?

We have an internal timeline: pilot (Jan) -> scale (Mar) with a decision point in Feb. We expect to start with ~1M monthly requests in pilot but the token mix is TBD.

Would prefer returning a completed spreadsheet if you have one.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Nguyen
Head of Platform, MLMarket Inc.
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@mlmarket.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit staging & burst profile — initial details

Sophie —

Thanks, this helps. Attached is our compact sizing workbook (redwood_sizing_workbook_v2.xlsx) — one tab per stage. If you can fill the pilot tab and add a couple of representative prompt/response examples we can run a quick footprint calc.

A few clarifying notes to save time:
- For burst sizing we ask for: peak requests/sec (p99) and sustained peak window length (minutes).
- Token lengths: please give median and 90th percentile for both prompt and response.
- Session shape: whether requests are short-lived (single-shot) or session-based (multi-turn with KV cache); if session-based, include average turns per session.
- Context windows: if you will switch models between 8k and 32k, indicate what fraction of traffic you expect on each.

I'll run an initial projection and follow up with a recommended staging plan (pilot dev nodes -> staged burst pool -> steady reserved). Marissa, Karthik — tagging you for pricing sensitivity and GPU SKU guidance.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sizing_workbook_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 98KB)
From: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@mlmarket.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@mlmarket.io
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit staging & burst profile — initial details

Ben —

Attached is our initial fill of the pilot tab and a short PDF with sample prompt/response pairs. Key points:
- Pilot expected request volume: 1.1M/mo (~0.38 rps average) but p95 business-hour QPS ~20, p99 bursts up to 160 for ~3 minutes.
- Median prompt tokens: 45; median response tokens: 120; 90th percentile prompt: 220; response 900 (we have some long summarization jobs).
- 65% session-based traffic (avg 6 turns), rest single-shot. KV cache reuse expected for 60% of session turns.
- 70% of traffic on 8k contexts, 30% occasional 32k long-form summaries.

We included a column estimating token growth during scale (Mar) to ~4.5M monthly when additional endpoints turn on.

Let me know if you need sample traces or a small anonymized dataset.

Thanks,
Sophie

Attachments: mlmarket_sizing_answers.pdf (58KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@mlmarket.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit staging & burst profile — initial details

Sophie —

Appreciate the quick turn. High-level takeaways from our side:
- Pilot footprint estimate (conservative): 1 x A100-equivalent node pool with autoscale headroom to handle p99 burst (we'd use burst credits from a shared burst pool during pilot for short spikes).
- For scale target (~4.5M/month) we project a tiered reserved fleet: base reserved for sustained QPS + a staged burst pool sized to absorb combined p99 across regional peak windows.
- Long-response jobs (900 tokens) materially increase memory and KV cache pressure; we'll recommend a quantization + batching strategy for those endpoints.

Marissa — we should prepare two offer lines: pilot reserved (low-term, small commit + burst credit bucket) and enterprise commit (12-month, staged capacity with predictable monthly billing). Karthik — any immediate constraints on GPU SKU availability for Jan pilot?

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie@mlmarket.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit staging & burst profile — initial details

Sophie —

Quick note on commercial options:
- Pilot package: 3-month term, minimal reserved baseline (30% of projected sustained), plus a 100k-token/month burst credit bucket and on-demand burst up to an agreed p99 for scheduled windows. Discount: 10% list during pilot.
- Enterprise commit: 12-month, baseline aligned to scaled sustained QPS; staged burst pool included. We can add an SLA for availability and latency p95.

I'll draft a short A/B pricing appendix and attach as a plain text draft for contracts. Ben/Karthik — I'll need the node SKU callout and a short note listing the recommended quantization/batching levers to include in the appendix.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sophie Nguyen <sophie@mlmarket.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit staging & burst profile — initial details

All —

Quick availability check: A100-equivalent pool for Jan pilot is feasible but lead time for full reserved nodes is ~6 weeks for guaranteed inventory in the primary us-west region. For pilot we can provision on a flexible dedicated pool with soft guarantees; for enterprise commit we'll map to an M60-X2 SKU (mixed precision friendly) and provide a quantization profile that typically saves 25-35% memory on 900-token responses.

Ben — I'll link the short SKU/quantization note I'm attaching to the HubSpot deal. Marissa — happy to review the A/B appendix before it goes to legal.

Karthik
